always_public.why: Amounts are fixed denominations, so they say little when other people move the same amount. The fewer such moves, the less they hide.
When you deposit, claim, burn and release is visible. Spreading the steps out is the protection.

always_public.item: An exit commitment and the burned denomination
always_public.why: The commitment hides your Ethereum recipient.

always_public.item: The release recipient, relayer and relay fee
always_public.why: Public by construction. The relay fee is 0 or a value from the vault's fixed menu, so it does not fingerprint you.

always_public.where: the RPC and sequencer you use
always_public.why: Outside the bridge's protection. Use endpoints you trust, or your own.

value.headline: Less private. The choices below make you easier to match by timing or pattern.
value.on_chain_error_text: If a claim is refused on chain, the only message anyone sees is "claim refused": it never says which deposit. The detailed reason shown here is worked out on this computer and is not sent.

overrides.leaks: A claim into a public account publishes the deposit's secret, which ties your Ethereum deposit (and the address that paid for it) to this LEZ account for good. A burn from a public account shows which account burned. Neither can be undone.
overrides.title: Use a public account

overrides.leaks: The bridge only moves standard amounts. Anything left over stays where it is; sending it some other way would fingerprint you.
overrides.title: Keep an amount that is not a standard denomination

overrides.leaks: Paying the release's gas yourself means the release transaction comes from an Ethereum address you funded. That address's history can identify you. A relayer, paid a fixed fee from the menu, avoids this.
overrides.title: Release on Ethereum myself (no relayer)

overrides.leaks: The release recipient is public on Ethereum by construction. Sending to an address linked to your identity (an exchange deposit address, your main wallet) tells everyone who received the money, though not which burn paid it.
overrides.title: Release to an address that is already mine and known

stays_private: Your LEZ account (for a private burn)

weakened_by.leaks: Paying the release's gas yourself means the release transaction comes from an Ethereum address you funded. That address's history can identify you. A relayer, paid a fixed fee from the menu, avoids this.
weakened_by.title: Release on Ethereum myself (no relayer)
